title: Reward Top K Students
summary: Given two string arrays, positive_feedback and negative_feedback, containing words that denote positive and negative feedback respectively (with no word being both positive and negative), and an array of feedback reports report along with an array student_id indicating the ID of the student for each report, calculate the points for each student.
statement: Given two string arrays, positive_feedback and negative_feedback, containing words that denote positive and negative feedback respectively (with no word being both positive and negative), and an array of feedback reports report along with an array student_id indicating the ID of the student for each report, calculate the points for each student. Each positive word in a feedback report increases a student's points by 3, and each negative word decreases the points by 1. Initially, every student has 0 points. Return the top k students in non-increasing order of their points, with ties broken by their student IDs.
constraints: Positive and negative vocabularies are disjoint.
A positive word scores +3, a negative word -1, and every other report word zero.
Return the top k student IDs by descending score and then ascending ID.
hints: Each report can be reduced to one numeric score.
Use sets for feedback lookup, then sort score-ID records by (-score,ID).
Tokenize every report, accumulate weights, sort, and return the first k IDs.
The sort key exactly encodes the primary descending score rule and secondary ascending-ID tie rule.
editorial: The sort key exactly encodes the primary descending score rule and secondary ascending-ID tie rule.

tests.explanation: Both students score three, so ID one ranks first.
